# What Agentic OCR Actually Is {#sec-what-it-is}

::: {.callout-note title="Executive summary" appearance="simple"}
- *(Phase C)*
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Drafter guidance" appearance="minimal"}
Target ~3,000 words. See `research/00-book-outline.md` Chapter 3. The five-attribute scorecard is the load-bearing artifact of this chapter — it gets referenced by every later chapter.

## Definition

- Working definition (single sentence): *Agentic OCR is a document-processing system that is goal-driven, multi-pass, self-correcting, tool-using, and grounded.*
- All five attributes must be present. Three of five is "VLM with retries," not agentic OCR.
- Why the definition matters: the term is being load-bearing in 2026 marketing and procurement decisions.

## The five attributes

### Goal-driven

- Operates against a **structured target** (a schema, an extraction goal, a downstream contract), not just "extract the text."
- Plan-then-execute behavior. The system can articulate what it's looking for before it looks.
- Anti-pattern: a model that emits markdown and hopes the downstream system figures it out.

### Multi-pass

- Iterates rather than emits-and-exits. At least one self-review pass.
- Includes the possibility of re-extraction with revised strategy (not just re-running the same prompt).
- The "loop" is not optional. A single-pass VLM is not agentic, even if it scores well.

### Self-correcting

- Three subsystems: **detection** (knowing you're wrong), **repair** (fixing it), **escalation** (failing safely). Full treatment in Chapter 5.
- Crucial: detection without ground truth is a model talking to itself. Real self-correction needs an external oracle (tool output, schema validation, or HITL).

### Tool-using

- Invokes specialized tools: layout detectors, table extractors, OCR for region, schema validators, external lookups (KB, normalization).
- Why this matters: leaderboards in 2026 show specialization beats generality at the high-stakes margin (Reducto on RD-TableBench, PP-StructureV3 at <100M params).
- Tool-using ≠ "the LLM has access to a function call." It means the model **routinely** invokes tools as part of its workflow, and the workflow is designed around that.

### Grounded

- Every output field can be traced back to a region of the source document.
- Why this matters beyond compliance: grounding is what makes self-correction's *detection* step possible. You cannot critique an answer you cannot localize.
- ParseBench's grounding dimension and Reducto's hybrid architecture both treat grounding as load-bearing, not optional.

## What it is not

- **Classic OCR with a confidence threshold.** Confidence gating is a feature of agentic OCR, not the definition.
- **A single-pass VLM.** Even GPT-4V on a document is not agentic; it is one extraction call.
- **Template-bound IDP with an LLM cleanup step.** This is wrapper-washing (Chapter 13). The template is still load-bearing; the LLM is decoration.
- **An LLM with one function-calling tool.** Tool-using means routinely-orchestrated, not technically-possible.

## The five-attribute scorecard

A 5-row, 3-column comparator (classic OCR / single-pass VLM / true agentic) marking each attribute Yes / No / Partial. Use this everywhere a vendor demo claims "agentic" and you want a defensible counter.

## Named takes

> *"'Agentic' is the word that lets people charge 10× for a retry loop. The five-attribute test exists so you don't get fooled."*

> *"Grounding is the line. If your system can't point at the pixels that produced a field, it isn't doing agentic OCR — it's doing confident hallucination."*
